transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Mark Liu (Acme CTO), Sara Gomez (ML Eng), Evan Park (Platform Lead), Lisa Tran (Product)

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for making time. i'm jordan from redwood, ae on the acme account. priya, do you wanna intro quickly?
00:08 Priya: yeah hi all, priya desai, solutions engineer. i'll be steering the demo portion and showing mapping from openai/anthropic and together calls to redwood's api and console.
00:16 Mark: great, we are curious about how much lift to migrate and whether things like function calling and streaming behave the same, and of course cost.
00:25 Jordan: perfect. quick agenda: 1) mapping parity 2) live demo of api + console 3) discuss dedicated/private options and security 4) q&a and next steps.
00:34 Priya: jumping in  first, high level: redwood exposes a compatible generation endpoint for text/chat, separate endpoint for embeddings, and supports streaming and function/tool calls. for many teams we provide a fairly direct translation layer.
00:47 Sara: so for example our current code calls openai.ChatCompletion.create with gpt-4o-mini, we do streaming and function calls to extract structured data. how would that look in redwood?
00:59 Priya: good question. for chat streaming you switch to POST /v1/chat/completions on redwood and you can set stream=true. model names are slightly different, we have a model catalog like redwood/gpt4o-mini-equivalent  we include a parity table (we'll share) that maps openai names -> redwood equivalents, and anthropic names -> redwood equivalents.
01:16 Jordan: i'll send the parity sheet after this call. but note: for function calling we support a JSON schema-based tool calling pattern similar to openai's. there are small differences in how we return function calls in the payload (and sometimes the type fields), so the migration usually needs a thin adapter, but in many cases it's a config switch.
01:40 Mark: any caveats? like how do we handle streaming chunks and partial function call events?
01:46 Priya: streaming is identical in that you get token deltas as they are generated. function-call events come as an 'invocation' chunk, sometimes with truncated args if you stream  we have SDK helpers to reassemble. the transcription here might say 'kv cash' or something but in the console it's 'KV cache'  sorry for the mess.
02:02 Evan: we have a big prefix cache use-case for chat history, how does redwood's prefix caching and continuous KV cache compare  any changes to our architecture?
02:12 Priya: redwood supports KV cache and prefix caching out of the box. operationally you can enable prefix caching by route, and the runtime will manage KV snapshots. the only time you change code is if you were manually managing a cache in your app; otherwise it's transparent.
02:28 Sara: embeddings  we use openai embeddings for semantic search, vector DB. what are model names and maintenance windows?
02:35 Priya: embeddings are on a separate endpoint /v1/embeddings, models like redwood/text-embedding-001-equivalent. we provide embedding dimensionality and stability docs. we also expose migration helpers: if you pass the same normalization pipeline, the vectors are comparable but you should run a small quality check.
02:52 Jordan: also want to call out cost/latency. many folks see token-cost reductions with quantized variants in dedicated deployments. for hosted api we'll show price numbers in the sheet but typical savings depend on batch patterns and caching.
03:06 Mark: can you demo the console? we wanna see rollout, tracing, and the per-route latency breakdown.
03:12 Priya: sure  i'm going to share my screen now.
03:18 [screen share starts]
03:20 Priya: this is the redwood console. top-left is the model catalog; i'm selecting a candidate model that maps to your current one. you can pin model versions per route. here is a per-route dashboard  tokens, latency p50/p95, and a cost breakdown. we also have a request inspector where you can replay a request and toggle model variants.
03:40 Lisa: that replay feature seems useful for regressions  can we compare outputs from openai and redwood side-by-side?
03:47 Priya: yes we have a diff tool  you can run the same prompt against multiple model variants and get a token-by-token diff, plus a quality metric if you provide reference labels.
03:58 Mark: what about rollouts  can we do canary + automatic fallback to anthropic/openai if latency spikes?
04:06 Jordan: we support policy-based routing. you can do region-based, latency-based or cost-tier fallback. if you want automatic fallback to an external vendor as a safety net, that is doable via our routing layer  you configure a primary route to redwood and a fallback to openai with pre-defined budgets.
04:20 Evan: hmm interesting, we'd probably want a fallback for critical flows. what's the auth story for private deployments?
04:26 Priya: for Private we support a private control plane and customer-managed networking, SSO/SAML for the console, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integration for key management. audit logs are exportable. SOC2 and ISO certs are available; i'll drop the security pack.
04:42 Sara: curious about latency  if we keep streaming and short context windows, can you meet our 100ms p50 target for single-turn?
04:50 Priya: p50 depends on model size and deployment. on dedicated gpu pools we routinely hit 60-80ms p50 for small generation models, but larger context windows and big models push that up. we'll need a benchmark on your exact prompt shapes.
05:05 Jordan: example: for chat with 2k context using a quantized variant on dedicated, our p95 is usually under 500ms in our tests. again, we'll run a bench with your traces.
05:16 Mark: what about throughput for embeddings  our nightly index job runs 200k embeddings per hour.
05:22 Priya: for bulk embedding jobs, we recommend batch endpoints and dedicated capacity. we can provision burst capacity, or you can run worker pools hitting hosted endpoints with rate limits. we'll include cost estimates in the pricing sheet.
05:35 Lisa: any gotchas moving from anthropic? we use claude for some assistant style tasks.
05:41 Priya: anthropic models have different safety framing; for assistant-style tasks you'll want to tune system prompts. redwood's models come with safety defaults, and our eval toolkit helps you measure behavior changes. the migration is often prompt engineering plus a small set of unit tests.
05:57 [05:57-10:30 Demo continued: Priya runs sample code snippets]
06:00 Priya: code snippet  node sdk example: const resp = await redwood.chat.create({model: 'redwood/gpt4o-alt', messages, stream:true}); // same pattern as openai, little change
06:16 Priya: php/java/python examples in the docs. for function calls, here's the schema payload. note: our sdk returns function calls in a field called 'tool_call' in the first stab here; older transcriptions sometimes rename things, but our current sdk is stable.
06:36 Sara: okay  so practically we probably need to add an adapter layer for the function call field names and maybe minor schema tweaks. seems fine.
06:45 Priya: yep. next, let's look at the console's optimize suggestions  this is the Optimize module. it analyzes your request distribution and suggests batching, cache TTLs, and model quantization profiles.
06:59 [07:00-09:30  console shows Optimize recommendations: batch size, cache TTL, quantization profile]
07:05 Priya: here it recommends batching of 16 for embedding bulk jobs and a TTL of 6h for prefix cache to save 18% on token spend. it's empirical based on your trace shape.
07:20 Jordan: we've seen customers reduce per-token costs by 15-35% after applying recommendations, especially combining prefix cache + dedicated quantized models.
07:33 Mark: about security again  are audit logs tamper-proof? we need chain of custody for some regulated data.
07:40 Priya: logs are tamper-evident, with append-only export and support for pushing to your SIEM. for private deploys you can keep logs on-prem.
07:50 Evan: scaling  how does autoscaling work for Dedicated? spikes in traffic  any cold start latency?
07:57 Priya: Dedicated is capacity-reserved so cold starts are minimal; autoscaling policies control GPU counts, and we have burst capacity options. for hosted you might see more cross-tenant throttling during huge spikes but we provide quotas and soft limits.
08:12 [08:12-14:30  Priya steps through sample benchmark spreadsheet and cost model]
08:15 Priya: final demo bit  here's the replay of a sample prompt and side-by-side diff against openai. you can flag regression and tie it back to eval tests.
08:32 Lisa: nice. what is the expected timeline to get a POC running? we have some compliance windows in late may.
08:38 Jordan: typical POC is 2-4 weeks: week 0 onboard + security checks, week 1-2 run benchmarks + iterate on prompts, week 3 evaluation and go/no-go. we can compress if needed.
08:51 Mark: cost model  can you show an example for our usage?
08:55 Priya: yes i'll run a quick estimate: if you run 200k embeddings/hour and 50k chat requests/day with 1.2k avg tokens, initial estimate points to 20-30% cost savings on dedicated quantized instances; hosted savings are smaller but still material with caching. detailed numbers in the spreadsheet.
09:15 [09:15-50:30  Q&A on integration specifics, Priya references a shared drive doc: https://redwood.ai/shared/acme-migration-deck ]
09:20 Mark: can you send us sample curl hooks and a migration checklist?
09:25 Jordan: yes, we'll send SDK snippets, a migration checklist, and the parity mapping spreadsheet.
09:30 Sara: one more  developer experience: will my devs need to learn a lot of new libs?
09:35 Priya: our SDKs mimic openai patterns deliberately; most devs are productive in a day or two. plus we provide code templates and quickstart repos.
09:45 Mark: is there an SLA for hosted customers?
09:49 Jordan: hosted API has a standard SLA we can include; Dedicated and Private come with higher SLA options as part of contracts.
09:55 Lisa: ok sounds good. let's recap next steps.
50:30 Jordan: recap  we'll send pricing, parity sheet, security pack, and schedule a POC kickoff. action items as listed.
50:45 Priya: adding one note  if you want to trial Private, we can do an air-gapped demo or a VPC peering trial; that takes a bit more time for network setup.
50:55 Mark: thanks everyone, this was helpful. we'll pull together sample workloads and confirm POC week.
51:05 Jordan: thanks  i'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
51:12 [call ended]
references: parity-sheet.csv (will be shared via CRM link)
